title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask a friend if they're free, suggest what to do, agree where and when to meet, say you're on your way or running late, and cancel without upsetting anyone.
intro:
Welcome to **Part 2**. From here on the course is about real life: the Telugu you need with friends, around town and at work. Making plans in Telugu means a lot of **పద, వెళ్దాం** ('come on, let's go'), a lot of English words with Telugu grammar (**ఫ్రీ**, **బిజీ**, **లేట్**, **వెయిట్ చెయ్**, **క్యాన్సిల్ చేద్దాం**), and the famous **ఐదు నిమిషాల్లో వచ్చేస్తా!** ('I'll be there in five minutes!'), often said by someone still at home.

You'll learn the everyday ways to say 'let's' and 'shall we?', how to boss your friends around with the informal command (and the **-రా / -వే** that close friends add), and how to say you're about to leave, on your way, or stuck in traffic. From now on, with friends, you'll also use the short spoken forms you met in Unit 20: *ఉన్నా*, *వస్తా*, *చెప్తా*.

English loan · బిజీగా ఉన్నా = I'm busy · far more common in speech than the native పనిలో ఉన్నా
ఖాళీగా ఉన్నా = I'm free / doing nothing · ఖాళీ సీటు = an empty seat
ఈ వీకెండ్ = this weekend
…ఏ మూడ్ లేదు = I don't feel like …-ing: సినిమాకి వెళ్ళే మూడ్ లేదు
To one friend. To a group or politely: పదండి · to a group of friends: పదండ్రా

vocab.en: aunty (a friend's mother, any older woman)
vocab.note: English loan, used with మీరు and -ండి · uncle: అంకుల్
పార్టీ ఇవ్వు = to throw a party / treat everyone
మా గ్యాంగ్ = my lot, my friends
Vizag's RK Beach is the classic hangout
English loan; in speech much more common than సిద్ధం · రెడీగా ఉండు = be ready · రెడీ అవు = get ready
Informal command: వెయిట్ చెయ్ · polite: వెయిట్ చేయండి · the native verb is ఆగు
నిన్ను పికప్ చేస్తా = I'll pick you up
The person reminded is in the dative: నాకు గుర్తు చెయ్ = remind me
After the oblique form: నా కోసం, నీ కోసం, బస్సు కోసం
Very colloquial · పక్కా వస్తా = I'll definitely come
లేట్ అవు = be / get late: లేట్ అయింది = I'm late · లేట్ చేయు = to be slow, make others late · native: ఆలస్యం
ట్రాఫిక్ జామ్ = traffic jam
ఇరుక్కుపోయా = I'm stuck (lit. I got stuck)
With a past verb = 'just': ఇప్పుడే వచ్చా = I've just arrived
ఏడు గంటల కల్లా = by seven o'clock

vocab.en: up to, as far as, until
vocab.note: The everyday word for వరకు: ఇంటి దాకా, రాత్రి దాకా
Doubling a question word asks for a list: ఎక్కడెక్కడ (where all), ఏమేమి (what all)
ఫిక్స్! = done, it's settled · ఫిక్స్ చేయు = to fix (a time, a plan) · ఫిక్స్ అవు = to be fixed

phrases.en: I'll be there in five minutes.
Sorry man, I can't make it today. (to a male friend)
phrases.note: To a female friend: సారీ వే... · politely: సారీ అండి, ఈరోజు రాలేను.

grammar.title: Let's, shall we, and 'we could just…'
grammar.body:
You met **-దాం** ('let's') and **-దామా?** ('shall we?') in Unit 17: *వెళ్దాం*, *తిందాం*, *చూద్దాం*, *కలుద్దామా?* Here is how friends actually use them.

**Start with పద.** *పద* (to one friend), *పదండి* (to a group, or politely), *పదండ్రా* (to a group of friends) is 'come on', and nearly every suggestion starts with it: *పద, బిర్యానీ తిందాం*.

**పోదాం = వెళ్దాం.** In everyday speech 'let's go' is very often *పోదాం* (from పో, 'go'), especially in Telangana and Hyderabad.

**'We could just…' / 'why don't we…'**: verb + **-ఒచ్చు కదా?** ('can, right?'): *ఇంట్లోనే సినిమా చూడొచ్చు కదా?* = we could just watch a film at home, no? It's softer than a straight 'let's'.

**'We're thinking of…'**: put *అని* after the let's-form: *వెళ్దామని అనుకుంటున్నాం* (we're thinking of going).

**'Let's not'**: verbal noun + **వద్దు** (*బయట తినడం వద్దు*), or just **వద్దులే** ('nah, let's not').

The trap: *వెళ్తాం* (we'll go) states a plan; to suggest it, say *వెళ్దాం* or *వెళ్దామా?*

examples.en: Shall we go to the beach this evening?
We could just watch a film at home, no?
We're thinking of going to Golconda on Saturday.

grammar.title: Talking to friends: commands, -రా / -వే, and switching to polite
grammar.body:
With friends you use **నువ్వు** and the **bare stem** as a command (Unit 11): *రా* (come), *చెప్పు* (tell), *ఉండు* (stay, be), *చూడు* (look). In speech **చేయి** is shortened to **చెయ్** (chey) and **వేయి** to **వెయ్**: *వెయిట్ చెయ్*, *ఫోన్ చెయ్*.

**-రా and -వే.** Close friends tag a command or question with **రా** to a man and **వే** (or **ఏ**) to a woman: *రారా* (come on, man), *చెప్పవే* (tell me, girl), *ఏంటే?* (what is it?). These are affectionate between equals but rude to anyone older or to a stranger. To a group of friends, add -రా to the plural: *రండ్రా*, *పదండ్రా*.

**Must, with friends.** **-ఆలి** ('must') makes a firm friendly order: *టైంకి రావాలి!* (you'd better be on time!).

**Don't**: stem + **-కు**: *లేట్ చేయకు* (don't be late), *మర్చిపోకు* (don't forget).

**Switch instantly** to **మీరు** and **-ండి** when a friend's parent or an older person joins in: *అంకుల్, కూర్చోండి*. Using *రా* with them would be shocking.

examples.en: Hey, still not ready? (to a female friend)
Come on, guys, it's getting late.
You'd better be on time, OK?
Uncle, please sit down, Ravi will be here in a moment.

grammar.title: About to leave, just left, on my way
grammar.body:
**About to**: stem + **-బోతున్నా(ను)** (Unit 13): *బయలుదేరబోతున్నా* (I'm about to leave), *మొదలవబోతోంది* (it's about to start).

**Just did**: **ఇప్పుడే** + past: *ఇప్పుడే బయలుదేరా* (I've just left), *ఇప్పుడే వచ్చా* (I've just got here). English says 'have just'; Telugu uses the plain past.

**On the way / coming**: *దారిలో ఉన్నా* (I'm on the way), *వస్తున్నా* (I'm coming). Friends love **వచ్చేస్తున్నా / వచ్చేస్తా**: the **-ఏస్-** inside adds 'right away, all the way' (more on these compound verbs in Unit 23).

**Late**: *లేట్ అవుతుంది* (I'll be late, lit. it will become late), *లేట్ అయింది* (I'm late), *అరగంట లేట్* (half an hour late). Native: *ఆలస్యం అవుతుంది*.

**Time limits**: **కల్లా** = by (*ఏడు కల్లా*, by seven), **దాకా** = until, as far as (*రాత్రి దాకా*).

examples.native: ఇప్పుడే బయలుదేరా, పది నిమిషాల్లో అక్కడ ఉంటా.
examples.roman: ippuḍē bayaludērā, padi nimiṣāllō akkaḍa uṇṭā.
examples.en: I've just left, I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.native: అమీర్‌పేట్ దగ్గర ట్రాఫిక్ జామ్, అరగంట లేట్ అవుతుంది.
examples.roman: amīrpēṭ daggara ṭrāphik jām, aragaṇṭa lēṭ avutundi.
examples.en: Traffic jam near Ameerpet, I'll be half an hour late.

dialogue.title: Evening at RK Beach
dialogue.setting: Visakhapatnam. Teja phones his friend Harsha to rope him into an evening at RK Beach with the gang.

lines.speaker: Teja
lines.en: Hello, Harsha! What're you up to, man?

lines.speaker: Harsha
lines.native: ఏమీ లేదు బావా, ఖాళీగా ఉన్నా. ఏంటి?
lines.roman: ēmī lēdu bāvā, khāḷīgā unnā. ēṇṭi?
lines.en: Nothing, bro, just chilling. What's up?

lines.speaker: Teja
lines.native: సాయంత్రం గ్యాంగ్ అంతా బీచ్‌కి వెళ్తున్నాం. నువ్వూ రా.
lines.roman: sāyantram gyāṅg antā bīchki veḷtunnām. nuvvū rā.
lines.en: The whole gang is going to the beach this evening. You come too.

lines.speaker: Harsha
lines.en: RK Beach? Who all is coming?

lines.speaker: Teja
lines.native: నేను, కీర్తి, సాయి... దివ్య కూడా వస్తానంది.
lines.roman: nēnu, kīrti, sāyi... divya kūḍā vastānandi.
lines.en: Me, Keerthi, Sai... Divya said she's coming too.

lines.speaker: Teja
lines.native: హహ, తెలుసులే. ఆరు గంటల కల్లా సబ్‌మెరైన్ దగ్గర కలుద్దాం. టైంకి రా, సరేనా?
lines.roman: haha, telusulē. āru gaṇṭala kallā sabmerain daggara kaluddām. ṭaimki rā, sarēnā?
lines.en: Ha, I know. Let's meet by the submarine by six. Be on time, OK?

lines.speaker: Harsha
lines.native: సరే సరే. నన్ను పికప్ చేస్తావా? నా బండి సర్వీసింగ్‌కి ఇచ్చా.
lines.roman: sarē sarē. nannu pikap chēstāvā? nā baṇḍi sarvīsiṅgki ichchā.
lines.en: OK, OK. Will you pick me up? My bike's in for servicing.

lines.speaker: Teja
lines.native: సరే, ఐదున్నరకి మీ ఇంటి దగ్గర ఉంటా. రెడీగా ఉండు!
lines.roman: sarē, aidunnaraki mī iṇṭi daggara uṇṭā. reḍīgā uṇḍu!
lines.en: Fine, I'll be at your place at half five. Be ready!

lines.speaker: Teja
lines.en: (At 5.30) Hey, where are you? I'm downstairs.

lines.speaker: Teja
lines.native: నీ ఒక్క నిమిషం నాకు తెలుసు! పదిహేను నిమిషాలైంది!
lines.roman: nī okka nimiṣam nāku telusu! padihēnu nimiṣālaindi!
lines.en: I know your 'one minute'! It's been fifteen minutes!

lines.speaker: Harsha
lines.en: Sorry, sorry, done. Come on, let's go!

culture: Plans among Telugu friends are made late and on the group chat: 'free tonight?' at five is normal. Time is elastic: *ఐదు నిమిషాల్లో వచ్చేస్తా* and *దారిలో ఉన్నా* are cheerfully said by people still at home, and twenty minutes' delay is barely worth a comment (offices, trains and weddings' auspicious times are another matter). A flat *రాను* ('I won't come') sounds harsh, so people soften it: *చూద్దాం* ('we'll see'), *వీలైతే వస్తా* ('I'll come if I can'), *ట్రై చేస్తా* ('I'll try'), all of which may mean no. Close friends call each other *రా* / *వే*, and young men say *బావా* or *మామా*; but if a friend's parent picks up the phone, switch at once to *మీరు*, *అండి* and *ఆంటీ / అంకుల్*. Favourite hangouts: in Hyderabad, Necklace Road, Tank Bund, the malls and late-night Irani cafés; in Vizag, RK Beach and Rushikonda; in Vijayawada, the Prakasam Barrage and Bhavani Island.

lessons.title: Asking if a friend is free

tip.title: Free? Busy? English words with Telugu grammar
tip.body:
- English adjectives take **-గా ఉండు**: **ఫ్రీగా** ఉన్నా, **బిజీగా** ఉన్నా.
- With a friend: **ఉన్నావా?** 'are you?' · with an elder or stranger: **ఉన్నారా?**
- Spoken 'I am': **ఉన్నా** (careful form ఉన్నాను).

sentences.en: Are you free tomorrow? (to a friend)

sentences.native: లేదు రా, ఈ వారం చాలా బిజీగా ఉన్నా.
sentences.roman: lēdu rā, ī vāram chālā bijīgā unnā.
sentences.en: No, man, I'm really busy this week.
What's the plan this weekend?
I'm free on Sunday.

sentences.native: ఆంటీ, మీరు ఈ వీకెండ్ ఖాళీగా ఉన్నారా?
sentences.roman: āṇṭī, mīru ī vīkeṇḍ khāḷīgā unnārā?
sentences.en: Aunty, are you free this weekend?
I'm not in the mood to go out today.
When are you free?
Sorry, busy right now, let's talk later.
You're always busy!

tip.title: Let's: పద … -దాం
tip.body:
- Let's: **-దాం** (వెళ్దాం, తిందాం); everyday 'let's go' is often **పోదాం**. Shall we? **-దామా?**
- Start with **పద** / **పదండి**: పద, తిందాం.
- We could just…: **-ఒచ్చు కదా?** ఇంట్లోనే చూడొచ్చు కదా?
- Let's not: **వద్దులే**, or verbal noun + **వద్దు**.

sentences.en: Come on, let's go to the mall.
Shall we meet at the beach this evening?
Why the bus? We could just take an auto, no?

sentences.native: గ్యాంగ్ అంతా శనివారం పార్టీకి వెళ్దామని అనుకుంటున్నాం.
sentences.roman: gyāṅg antā shanivāram pārṭīki veḷdāmani anukuṇṭunnām.
sentences.en: The whole gang is thinking of going to a party on Saturday.
Where's the party? At whose place?
Let's not eat out, let's just cook at home.
Nah, not the beach, let's go to the mall.
I'm in! When shall we set off?
Come on, is everyone ready?

tip.title: To a friend: the bare stem, plus రా / వే
tip.body:
- Informal command = the stem: **రా**, **చెప్పు**, **ఉండు**; చేయి is said **చెయ్**.
- Close friends add **-రా** (to a man) or **-వే** (to a woman): **రారా**, **చెప్పవే**. To a group: **రండ్రా**.
- To elders and strangers always **-ండి**: వెయిట్ **చేయండి**.

sentences.en: Wait for me at the bus station.

sentences.native: రేపు ఉదయం నాకు గుర్తు చెయ్, సరేనా?
sentences.roman: rēpu udayam nāku gurtu chey, sarēnā?
sentences.en: Remind me tomorrow morning, OK?

sentences.native: పదింటికి రెడీగా ఉండు, నేను పికప్ చేస్తా.
sentences.roman: padiṇṭiki reḍīgā uṇḍu, nēnu pikap chēstā.
sentences.en: Be ready at ten, I'll pick you up.
Come quickly, man, the film's going to start!
Come on, tell me, what's the plan? (to a female friend)
Come here, guys, let's take a photo!
Are you definitely coming? If not, tell me.
You're definitely coming, right?

sentences.native: మీ కోసం ఎంత సేపు వెయిట్ చేయాలి?
sentences.roman: mī kōsam enta sēpu veyiṭ chēyāli?
sentences.en: How long do we have to wait for you lot?
Sir, please wait a moment.

tip.title: About to, just left, on the way
tip.body:
- About to: **-బోతున్నా**: బయలుదేర**బోతున్నా**.
- Just did: **ఇప్పుడే** + past: ఇప్పుడే **ఎక్కా** 'I've just got on'.
- On the way: **దారిలో ఉన్నా** · coming right now: **వచ్చేస్తున్నా**, **వచ్చేస్తా**.
- By (a time): **కల్లా**: ఏడు గంటల **కల్లా**.

sentences.en: I'm about to leave the office.
I've just got on the bus.
I'm on my way, another ten minutes.

sentences.native: సారీ, ట్రాఫిక్ ఎక్కువగా ఉంది, లేట్ అయింది.
sentences.roman: sārī, ṭrāphik ekkuvagā undi, lēṭ ayindi.
sentences.en: Sorry, there's a lot of traffic, I'm late.
I'll be there by seven.
I'm on the train, I'll be there in another half hour.
Hey, you haven't left yet?

sentences.native: ఐదు నిమిషాల్లో వచ్చేస్తా అన్నావు, గంట అయింది!
sentences.roman: aidu nimiṣāllō vachchēstā annāvu, gaṇṭa ayindi!
sentences.en: You said you'd be here in five minutes, it's been an hour!
I'm stuck in traffic, you guys go ahead and eat.

tip.title: Meeting up: where, when, who
tip.body:
- Where shall we meet? **ఎక్కడ కలుద్దాం?** · at the temple: **గుడి దగ్గర**.
- Clock times in speech: **ఏడింటికి** 'at seven', **ఆరున్నరకి** 'at half six'.
- Who all? Double the question word: **ఎవరెవరు**.
- Done deal: **ఫిక్స్!** · until / as far as: **దాకా**.

sentences.en: Where shall we meet? At the bus station?
OK, seven o'clock at the temple. Done!
Who all is coming to the party?
Who all needs tickets?
Let's fix a time.
The film's from eight till eleven.

sentences.native: మీ ఇంటి దాకా వస్తా, అక్కడి నుంచి కలిసి వెళ్దాం.
sentences.roman: mī iṇṭi dākā vastā, akkaḍi nunchi kalisi veḷdām.
sentences.en: I'll come over to your place, and we'll go together from there.
Six or half six, which works for you?
Is the plan fixed?

tip.title: Saying no nicely
tip.body:
- A flat **రాను** 'I won't come' sounds rude. Soften it: **సారీ రా, రాలేను** 'sorry, I can't'.
- Hedge: **చూద్దాం** 'we'll see', **వీలైతే వస్తా** 'if I can': often a polite no.
- Offer another time: **వేరే రోజు చూద్దాం**, **వచ్చేసారి పక్కా!**

sentences.native: సారీ రా, ఆఫీసులో పని ఎక్కువైంది, రాలేను.
sentences.roman: sārī rā, āphīsulō pani ekkuvaindi, rālēnu.
sentences.en: Sorry, man, there's too much work at the office, I can't come.
Shall we cancel the plan?
It rained, so the party got cancelled.
You could have told me earlier!
Well then, let's do it another day.
We'll see, I'll come if I can.
Sorry this time, next time I'll definitely come!

sentences.native: నాకు ఒంట్లో బాగాలేదు, ఈరోజు క్యాన్సిల్ చేద్దాం.
sentences.roman: nāku oṇṭlō bāgālēdu, īrōju kyānsil chēddām.
sentences.en: I'm not feeling well, let's cancel today.
No worries, man, we'll meet another time.
